metaDescription: Five cool-touch electric griddles compared by cooking area, surface coating, grease handling and storage size, from compact 10.5-inch to 20-inch models.
introParagraphs: A cool-touch electric griddle gives you a flat cooking surface for pancakes, eggs and French toast without hauling out a stovetop pan. The cool-touch base is the headline safety feature, because the sides and front stay more comfortable to brush against than a bare metal housing. The cooking plate itself still gets very hot, so the label means a safer edge and not a cold griddle.

This lineup is made up mostly of Presto models, which is the brand most closely tied to the term, along with one compact Elite Gourmet. They differ mainly in cooking area, from the 10.5 by 8.5 inch Elite Gourmet up to the 20 inch Presto 07030. Grease handling also splits the group, with a tilt-and-drain design on one and a flip-back tray on another.

We evaluated these picks based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at plate size, coating, heat control and storage. No prices appear because they change. Start with how many people you cook for and how much counter and cupboard space you can spare. Then decide whether grease drainage or a warming tray matters more to your routine. Most buyers land on a mid-size plate, because the largest ones are awkward to store and the smallest need repeated batches. Whichever you pick, give it a stable, heat-safe spot and clear the area around the plate before you plug it in. Keep a pair of nylon tongs and a flexible spatula nearby so the coating lasts. A damp cloth within reach makes wiping easy once the plate has cooled. Allow room behind the unit so steam and heat can escape safely. Never leave a heated griddle unattended.

products.name: Presto 07047 16-Inch Cool Touch Electric Griddle
products.description:
The 07047 hits the middle of the lineup on both size and features. It offers a generous 10.5 by 16 inch cooking area with a built-in backstop ledge, which stops pancakes and eggs from sliding off the back edge. The cool-touch base wraps the front and sides, so you can brush against the housing without worrying about the metal.

Its PFAS-free ceramic nonstick surface supports easy release and quick wipe-downs. That coating asks for gentle tools, so use nylon or wood rather than metal utensils. The size suits a household of two to four, with enough room for a few pancakes or several eggs at once.

It does not tilt to drain grease like the 07046, and it lacks the warming tray of the 07023. Compared with the 20-inch 07030, it takes less room on the counter and in a cupboard. Against the compact Elite Gourmet at 10.5 by 8.5 inches, it nearly doubles the cooking area. Cleanup is a wipe-down after the plate cools, and the ledge catches stray batter. It is the safe default for people who want one griddle that suits most breakfasts.
products.bestFor: Households of two to four who want a balanced size and a cool-touch edge.

products.name: Presto 07030 20-Inch Cool Touch Electric Griddle
products.description:
Presto 07030 is the largest cooker here and the one for feeding a crowd. Its 20 inch surface is described as great for every meal, so it handles pancakes at breakfast and burgers or quesadillas later. A low-profile design is listed for buffet serving, which keeps the cooking area easy to reach and serve from.

The ceramic nonstick surface is PFAS free, and the cool-touch construction keeps the outer body safer to bump against. The sheer size means you can cook several items at different spots on the plate. A griddle this large also suits holiday mornings when the whole family is eating at the table.

The tradeoff is storage, since a 20 inch plate does not slip into a small cupboard easily. The brief gives no grease channel or drain feature, so cooking bacon means wiping up more. Compared with the 07047 at 16 inches, it adds area but also weight and bulk. Against the 07046 Tilt n Drain, it lacks the draining angle. Pick it if you routinely cook for four or more people.

products.name: Presto 07046 Tilt 'n Drain Big Griddle
products.description:
The 07046 is built around a clever adjustment: it sits level for pancakes and tilts to drain fat from meats. Presto says the huge cooking area holds up to 12 slices of French toast at a time. That flexibility is what sets it apart from the flat-only models here.

The tilt means bacon grease runs to one side instead of pooling under the food. For people who cook sausages, burgers or bacon, that is a real improvement in both cooking and cleanup. The cool-touch exterior keeps the base safer to handle while the plate heats.

The tradeoff is complexity, since a tilting mechanism is another part to learn and keep clean. It takes up a big footprint, like the 07030, so check your storage. Compared with the 07047, it gives you drainage rather than a backstop ledge. Against the 07023 with its warming tray, it focuses on grease management over keeping food warm. It suits cooks who prepare fatty foods and want less mess.

products.name: Presto 07023 Cool-Touch Griddle and Warmer Plus

specList.label: Tray
specList.value: Flips back, up, forward, or removes

products.description:
The 07023 stands out for its multi-function tray, which flips back to keep cooked food warm. The same tray flips up as a spatter shield, swings forward for melting and steaming, and can be removed altogether. That makes it the most versatile design in the group.

The 14 by 15 inch cooking surface is big enough for pancakes, eggs and grilled sandwiches. Presto calls it great for any meal, so the tray earns its keep with melted cheese or steamed vegetables. The cool-touch construction lets you reach around the unit without bumping hot metal.

The tradeoff is that the multi-position tray adds parts to clean and a mechanism you must learn. It is not as wide as the 20 inch 07030 or as tall in capacity as the 07046. Compared with the compact Elite Gourmet, it adds the warmer, but it also takes more shelf room. It suits cooks who want to serve food hot while the next batch is on the plate. The removable tray also helps with washing, since it can be taken to the sink separately. Keep that in mind if you hate cleaning awkward corners.

products.name: Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B Cool-Touch Griddle
products.description:
The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B is the smallest griddle in the group and the easiest to put away. Its non-stick surface measures 10.5 by 8.5 inches, and the 1200 watt element heats in minutes with a thermostat that adjusts up to 425 degrees F. The listing calls the cool-touch design suitable for personal or family prep.

It cooks pancakes, French toast, eggs, bacon, burgers, grilled cheese and quesadillas, so the small plate still handles a range of meals. The 1200W rating is the only wattage figure given in this lineup. A compact body means less to store and less counter space used.

The tradeoff is area, because the plate is much smaller than the 16 inch 07047. You will cook in batches for more than two people. Compared with the 20 inch 07030, it uses a fraction of the space. It is a good fit for a solo cook or couple, a dorm or an apartment where counter room is scarce. Cleanup is quick because there is simply less plate to wipe. Set it on a heat-safe surface and let the plate cool fully before putting it away.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Plate size decides how many pancakes, eggs or sandwiches cook at once. The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B at 10.5 by 8.5 inches suits one or two people. The Presto 07047 offers 10.5 by 16 inches, the 07023 gives 14 by 15, and the 07030 stretches to 20 inches. Choose the smallest plate that still lets you cook in a single round, because bigger units cost storage room. A rule of thumb is to count the number of servings you want hot at the same moment and size up from there. Anything beyond that is counter space you pay for with every cleaning.

Cool-touch refers to the base and housing, not the cooking plate. The Presto 07047 lists a cool-touch base on the front and sides. The plate still reaches cooking temperatures, so keep pot holders handy and teach everyone to treat it as hot. Check that the cord and controls are positioned away from the cooking area. The Presto 07030 adds a low profile, which keeps the heated plate closer to table height. Always set the griddle on a stable, heat-safe surface well away from the counter edge.

Fatty foods need somewhere for grease to go. The Presto 07046 tilts so fat drains away, which suits bacon and burgers. Most flat models, like the 07030 and 07047, leave grease on the plate. If you cook a lot of meat, a drain design saves cleanup time. The Presto 07023 handles splatter differently, with a tray that flips up as a spatter shield. Paper towels and a little patience still do the rest, whichever design you choose.

A ceramic nonstick surface releases food easily but wants gentle tools. The Presto 07030 and 07047 both list PFAS-free ceramic surfaces. Use nylon or wooden utensils and avoid metal scrapers. Let the plate cool before cleaning to avoid stress on the surface. The 07046 Tilt n Drain and 07023 follow similar care rules for the cooking plate. Skip aerosol cooking sprays, which can leave a sticky film on ceramic over time.

Heat control determines whether eggs set gently or burn. The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B lists 1200 watts and a thermostat up to 425 degrees F. The Presto listings in this brief do not give wattage, so check the box. Look for a thermostat with clear settings you can read easily. At 425 degrees F the Elite Gourmet runs hot enough to sear a burger, while eggs and pancakes want a lower dial. Preheat for a few minutes before the first pour so the whole plate is even.

A griddle spends most of its life in a cupboard, so footprint matters. The 20 inch Presto 07030 takes the most room, while the Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B takes the least. Check shelf depth before buying a big plate. If you must lift it from a high shelf, consider a smaller model. The Presto 07047 and 07023 sit in the middle for both size and bulk. A lower shelf or a bottom drawer makes any of these safer to handle.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cooking area
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plate dimensions from each listing. The Presto 07030 leads at 20 inches, the 07047 follows at 10.5 by 16, and the Elite Gourmet is smallest at 10.5 by 8.5. Capacity claims like 12 slices of French toast on the 07046 were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cool-touch safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each listing describes the cool-touch construction. The Presto 07047 specifies the front and sides. We treated all plates as hot and scored on the edge safety only. Listings that did not describe where the cool-touch zone sits were scored with caution. No listing was credited with a safety claim it did not make.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grease and mess control
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed drain, ledge and tray designs. The 07046 tilts to drain, the 07047 has a backstop ledge, and the 07023 offers a spatter shield position. Flat models without those features scored lower. We also considered whether the design reduces wiping at the end of a meal. Mess control mattered more than raw plate size here.

howWeEvaluated.title: Surface and cleanup
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked coating claims and ease of wiping down. The 07030 and 07047 list PFAS-free ceramic surfaces, and the Elite Gourmet lists a non-stick plate. We noted that all coatings need gentle tools. Plates that can be wiped clean without scrubbing scored higher. Removable parts, such as the 07023 tray, were counted as a cleanup plus.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The 07047 leads on balance, the 07030 on size, the 07046 on grease, the 07023 on versatility and the Elite Gourmet on compactness. These positions guided our badges. Each badge reflects a single standout trait, not an overall ranking on every spec. Read the whole entry before choosing, since the best overall pick is not best for every kitchen.

faq.q: Does cool-touch mean the griddle stays cold?
faq.a: No, the cooking plate gets hot. Cool-touch refers to the base and housing. The Presto 07047 lists a cool-touch base on the front and sides. Always treat the plate as hot and keep hands away. Children and pets should be kept clear until the griddle has cooled completely. Unplug it after use and let it sit before moving it.

Match the plate to your household. The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B at 10.5 by 8.5 inches suits one or two. The Presto 07047 at 10.5 by 16 inches suits families, and the 07030 at 20 inches suits crowds. Consider storage as much as cooking area. If you only occasionally cook for a crowd, cooking in two rounds on the 07047 is usually easier than owning a 20 inch plate.

faq.q: How do I clean a ceramic nonstick griddle?
faq.a: Let it cool, then wipe with a soft sponge and mild soap. Avoid abrasive pads and metal tools. The Presto 07030 and 07047 list PFAS-free ceramic surfaces. Dry it fully before storing. Never immerse the control or cord connection in water. A drop of oil wiped across the plate now and then helps keep the surface slick.

faq.q: Is a tilt-and-drain griddle worth it?
faq.a: It is worth it for fatty foods. The Presto 07046 tilts so grease runs away from meat. If you mostly make pancakes and eggs, a flat griddle like the 07047 is simpler. Think about what you cook most. The extra mechanism is one more thing to clean and store. For occasional bacon, a paper-towel wipe on a flat plate may be enough.

faq.q: Can I use metal spatulas on these griddles?
faq.a: Ceramic coatings are best with nylon or wooden tools. Metal can scratch the surface. Use silicone or wood for safety. Check each manual before using anything sharp. A spatula with a thin, flexible edge works well on ceramic and makes flipping pancakes easier. Never cut food directly on the plate.

faq.q: What temperature should I cook pancakes at?
faq.a: A medium setting is typical, though each model differs. The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B lists an adjustable thermostat up to 425 degrees F. Presto models have their own controls, so follow the manual. Preheat before pouring batter. If the first pancake browns too fast, drop the dial and wait a minute before continuing.

faq.q: Why is the Presto 07023 different from the other models?
faq.a: It adds a tray that moves into several positions. It flips back to keep food warm, flips up as a spatter shield and swings forward for melting and steaming. It can also be removed for washing. That flexibility costs a few extra parts to learn and clean.

faq.q: Do I need a 20 inch griddle for a family?
faq.a: Usually not. The Presto 07047 at 10.5 by 16 inches handles a family breakfast in a round or two. The 20 inch 07030 is worth it if you often feed a crowd at once. Otherwise the smaller plate saves cupboard space and cleaning time.
